# Nodes

Every node a pipeline can use: a pure function of the data handed to it, with named input and output ports. Pipelines (see the [index](pipelines/README.md)) are chains of these nodes. The toolbox is the part of the name before the dot.

Kinds: accumulate: folds each chunk into a running result; after: runs once on the accumulated result; array: runs once on whole arrays; chunk: runs on every block of every chunk; setup: runs once, before the data flows.

Toolboxes: [geometry](#geometry) (9), [measurement](#measurement) (9), [meeg](#meeg) (34), [operators](#operators) (3), [select](#select) (23), [signal](#signal) (39), [stats](#stats) (12), [synthesis](#synthesis) (3).

## geometry

| node | kind | inputs (optional marked) | outputs | parameters (defaults) | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `geometry.frame_embed` | chunk | `x`, `grid` | `y` |  | z = a + ib at a vertex becomes the 3-vector a e1 + b e2 (tangent to the surface, gauge-free). Matches: an analytic embedding (tests): y = a e1 + b e2 |
| `geometry.frame_project` | chunk | `x`, `grid` | `y` |  | The inverse of geometry.frame_embed on the tangent plane: z = (v . e1) + i (v . e2); the part of v along the normal is dropped. Matches: an analytic projection (tests): z = (v . e1) + i (v . e2) |
| `geometry.frame_rotate` | chunk | `x`, `to` | `y` | `spin`=`0` | x e^(-i k to) per element: the components of a spin-k value on the frame whose reference lies at angle `to` in x's gauge (north's gauge angle gives (north, west) for k = 1; for k = 2 a line field's double angle is measured from north). Matches: an analytic rotation (tests): y = x e^(-i k to) |
| `geometry.glue` | setup | `surface`, `hemispheres` | `glued`, `labels` | `left`=`Cortex L`, `right`=`Cortex R` | a cortex of two hemispheres glued by anatomy into ONE closed surface: each medial wall cut out exactly (nothing more), a bridge of new vertices grown between the two rims. The hemispheres are the caller's labelling of the original (left and right named); makes the glued surface and its hemispheres labelling (the input's entries and `bridge`); refused when the labelling and the surface disagree Matches: the Studio's glue.ts glueMesh (nxr-compute glue.h; nxr geom.glue) |
| `geometry.intrinsic` | setup | `surface` | `triangulation`, `d0`, `d1`, `star0`, `star1`, `star2`, `length`, `angle_tail`, `angle_tip`, `angle_sum`, `reference` | `mollify`=`1e-06`, `flip_eps`=`1e-06` | the intrinsic Delaunay triangulation of a surface of one closed piece: its own edges and faces on the surface's positions, d0, d1 and the Hodge stars as analytic operators (method dec), the edge lengths and the signposts as fields on its cells Matches: the Studio's intrinsicDelaunay.ts (intrinsicMesh, mollify, flipToDelaunay) and hodgeDirac.ts dec(m); nxr-compute delaunay.h |
| `geometry.point_set_mesh` | setup | `points` | `faces` | `cut`=`2.0`, `pole`=`[0, 0, 1]`, `orientation`=`outward`, `repair_passes`=`20` | The triangles of a point set on a cap, every point a vertex: points [n x 3] -> faces [F x 3]. The points projected about the pole (an azimuthal equidistant map from their centroid), the planar Delaunay, triangles with an edge of cut x the median edge or longer removed, pinched vertices and holes repaired, each triangle turned outward (from the centroid) or left as_triangulated. Refused when a point is in no triangle. The mesh's topology (boundary loops, Euler characteristic) and what the repair did are in meta.mesh. Matches: nxr::geometry::pointset::pointSetMesh (nxr's sensor mesh: heatdist.sensor_mesh and SensorSurface's outward turn) |
| `geometry.surface_frames` | setup | `surface` | `canonical`, `singular`, `gauge_angle`, `angle`, `second`, `handed`, `reliable` | `template`=none, `template_surface`=none, `convention`=`scs`, `side`=`auto`, `min_projection`=`0.34`, `max_condition`=`50.0` | a surface's canonical frames (from its registered sphere) and its anatomical frame Matches: Rheome sphereframe (canonical frames); nxr coords.py anatomical frame; compute nxr::geometry |
| `geometry.surface_from_parts` | setup | `vertices`, `faces` | `surface` |  | Two arrays as a surface to store: vertices [V x 3] (meta.cs, the coordinate system) and faces [F x 3] (0-based indices) -> surface (the vertices, with the faces, the coordinate system and what the producing nodes recorded: meta.sensor_positions of the vertices, meta.mesh of the faces). The inverse of geometry.surface_parts. Matches: the surface's stored vertices and faces |
| `geometry.surface_parts` | setup | `surface` | `vertices`, `faces` |  | A surface as two arrays: vertices [V x 3] in the surface's unit (its precision and coordinate system in meta) and faces [F x 3] (0-based indices as doubles). Matches: the surface's stored vertices and faces |

| node | kind | inputs (optional marked) | outputs | parameters (defaults) | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `measurement.cellquadrature` | setup | `cross_spectrum`, `recording`, `kernel`, `joint`, `bursts`? | `cells`, `cell_pairs`, `bursts`, `burst_pairs` | `spatial_scale`=none, `weights`=`area`, `tile_pairs`=true, `transform`=`auto`, `modes`=none, `order`=none, `tolerance`=none | the quadrature ingredients of the kernel's spatial tiles (and touching tile pairs) per time tile of the joint cells and per burst, from an analytic cross-spectrum Matches: compute nxr::measurement::groupedCongruenceNorms, pairCongruenceNorms; the merge rule sum (nxr::measurement) |
| `measurement.collect` | accumulate | `x` | `y` |  | the own columns of every chunk appended: a [rows × samples] series of the span (MEMORY: rows × samples doubles, held until the run ends). A SERIES, not a reduction: what the sample-level fit (`risefall`) reads. Matches: the samples of the run kept in order (the chunk service's own columns): the trace at the recording's rate |
| `measurement.estimate` | accumulate | `x`, `exclude`?, `outside`? | `y` | `method`=none, `bad_segments`=`exclude`, `bins`=`4096`, `range_frames`=`3000`, `block_frames`=`256`, `edges`=none | a statistic from the stream, by `method`: `sample` = the mean over the good columns of x (the BASELINE of a band's power per vertex and level, left out: `exclude` the bad segments and `outside` the bursts; any other real field: its mean, samples cut by an excluded span counted); `histogram` = counts of the good frames' values: fixed bins when `edges` are given, else nxr's 4096 log bins (range from the first `range_frames` good frames) over \|curl\| of the current (the cores' threshold) or over the relative power outside the bursts (the patches' threshold). Welch's segments are `welch.*` nodes on SegmentMean. Matches: baseline: nxr-neuro's own (spec 2026-11-14-spatial-events.md, piece 1): the Studio's `mean` measure (reduceTiles) over a time Selection, folded chunk by chunk; the lookup's `mean` of a statistic; core_histogram: nxr vortex._core_threshold (4096 log bins, hi = 4 × the first chunk's maximum, lo = hi·1e-6; the first 3000 frames); compute nxr::stats::histogram (logBinsFor, histogramTiles); relative_histogram: the time burst detector's threshold from the envelope's own distribution; compute nxr::stats::histogram (logBinsFor, histogramTiles), as core_histogram; mean: nxr's Welch segment mean (scipy.signal.welch) and nxr's log-binned histograms; compute nxr::measurement::SegmentMean, Histogram; fixed: nxr's Welch segment mean (scipy.signal.welch) and nxr's log-binned histograms; compute nxr::measurement::SegmentMean, Histogram |
| `measurement.reduce` | accumulate | `x`, `over`?, `exclude`?, `weights`? | `values`, `ingredients` | `measures`=none, `weight`=`none`, `bad_segments`=`exclude` | A field reduced over the members of ANY selection (a time grid, a surface grid, a product of them, a channel set, the run's span as one member), per row, in ONE pass: the additive INGREDIENTS (count, weight, sum, sum of squares, max, min, largest magnitude; per component for a vector) are folded block by block, and the requested measures are read from them (`values`); the ingredients (`ingredients`) are what is stored and what rolls up (`roll_up`: a merge rule per measure, data in the measures registry). Ratios (an amplitude, an sd) are derived at read, never reduced themselves. A member cut by an excluded span or by the run's edge is NaN, never a short mean. `measures` has no default; `weight` is none, or the surface's barycentric (or voronoi) vertex areas for a member of a surface grid. Matches: the Studio's backend/src/db/measurements.ts reduceTiles and measureOverPartition (the measure registry, the lookup); compute nxr::measurement::reduce |
| `measurement.reduce_members` | after | `x`, `over` | `values`, `ingredients` | `measures`=none | the ingredients of a measurement over a grid's members merged over the members of an irregular selection given on them (each event's cells): the event's value from its cells' ingredients by each measure's merge rule (sums add, maxima merge), never a second pass over the signal. The events' members may overlap; no level, no roll-up. Matches: the Studio's measureOverPartition over a stored measurement; compute nxr::measurement::merge |
| `measurement.reduce_statistic` | after | `x`, `over` | `values` | `measures`=none | A stored statistic (a PSD [channels x frequencies]) reduced over the members of a selection of its first axis, by registry measures: one value per (row, member), the rows the statistic's other axes in order. The same reduction as a field's over a set of elements, so a channel set's mean spectrum is a measurement read by name, never a loop inside a node. Elements the selection does not hold (member -1) are left out. The measurement is OF the statistic. Matches: the Studio's measureOverPartition over a stored statistic's first axis; compute nxr::measurement::reduce (members of elements) |
| `measurement.relative` | chunk | `x`, `baseline` | `y` |  | x divided, row by row, by a stored per-row constant read BY NAME (`baseline`: a statistic of method mean, measure power): the band's power at each vertex in units of that vertex's own baseline power. A diagonal scaling bound once in preparation, pointwise in time and in space (it reduces across nothing). The baseline must be of the same chain (band, spatial band and levels, form, glue, frame tiling: a power divided by another chain's baseline is refused) and of x's rows; a baseline that is not above 0 at a row is refused. The result is unitless Matches: nxr-neuro's own (spec 2026-11-14-spatial-events.md, piece 2); compute nxr::core::divideRows (a diagonal scaling, general algebra) |
| `measurement.roll_up` | after | `x`, `grid`? | `values`, `ingredients` | `to`=none, `measures`=none, `factor`=`0`, `merge`=none | a measurement's ingredients carried up a GRID's closed-form hierarchy to a coarser level (`to`: a duration such as `2 s`, a tile size such as `40 mm`, `pieces`, or `whole`: one member; for a product, `factor` names the factor rolled): sums add, maxima merge, means by sum and count, ratios derived at read (the merge rule of each measure is data in the measures registry). Refused over an irregular selection (no levels). `merge: max` (a product's surface factor, one measure) takes instead the largest of the members' VALUES (the largest tile mean per time member: the series of the largest tile's mean, what the rise-fall fit reads; MEMORY: the product's cells, S x samples when the time factor is the sample). Matches: the Studio's measurement roll-up through a grid's hierarchy (the merge rule of each measure); compute nxr::measurement::roll_up |
| `measurement.summarize` | after | `x` | `y` | `summaries`=`["median", "mad"]`, `combine`=`each`, `ddof`=`1`, `measure`=none, `by_factor`=none | a measurement's members summarised into a STATISTIC (members -> statistic; across an irregular set it is a `summary`; never of a field): per row (each), pooled, or the mean over rows; NaN members are skipped and counted Matches: nxr::measurement::summarize (the summaries of compute nxr::stats: numpy median and linear percentile, Rheome's robust SD, MATLAB's sd, kurtosis, skewness) |

## meeg

| node | kind | inputs (optional marked) | outputs | parameters (defaults) | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `meeg.apply_kernel` | chunk | `x`, `kernel`, `tiles`?, `pre_operator`?, `glued`? | `y` | `spatial_scale`=none, `spatial_scales`=none, `transform`=`auto`, `modes`=`0`, `order`=`0`, `tolerance`=`0.01`, `envelope`=`temporal`, `spatial_shape`=`mexhat`, `form`=`none` | a linear operator from the field's first factor applied to it: x [members × time] → K x [target × time] (an imaging kernel: sensors → sources). `levels` (; instead of `level`) is ONE operator a hat level, all bound in preparation: the output is [vertex × level] (the rows of a vertex's levels consecutive, then a vertex's components: row = (vertex · levels + level) · components + component; `facts.levels` names them), the scale-space the spatial events' scale selection reads. `glued` (default false; a `form` is always glued) evaluates the band on EVERY vertex of the glued surface for a field with no form too (a free current: each component through the band, the bridge filled). `form` folds a LINEAR form of the free current into the same operator, in preparation: kernel (x y z a vertex) → its tangent part → curl_tan (or div_tan; `normal`: n·x) → the spatial band, ONE linear map before any non-linear step (D106); the output is ONE scalar a vertex (complex when x is: the analytic signal's curl; nxr vortex.Cortex.readings: div_curl(tangent(q)), then the hat of vortex_cores.hat_operator). With `tiles` the output is on EVERY vertex of the GLUED surface. With `tiles` (the target surface's tile ladder) and `level`: M x with M = (F_l ⊗ I) K, F_l the level's Weyl band on each component of the kernel's rows, bound ONCE in preparation (a linear map reads the chain before any non-linear step, D106; no graph filtering per sample). `envelope` temporal (the default: M x) \| spatiotemporal. `spatial_shape` mexhat \| meyer (the level IS its Weyl band: compact, the levels add up). `transform` auto, eigen, chebyshev (order 0: chosen from `tolerance`) or exact (dense modes of the mesh, ≤ 4096 vertices). `pre_operator` (optional): a linear operator on x's rows applied BEFORE the kernel (an array [M × M] over `meta.channels`, made by an earlier node: a surrogate's zero-lag mixing), COMPOSED once into the same operator (M · P, the type system's compose move; spec docs/specs/2026-11-17-surrogates.md, section 5); x then awaits it (`awaits_operator` names what the operator is of) and the mark is cleared. The bound operator is cached across runs by its inputs' provenance Matches: Studio adapters/nxr kernelOf (the kernel padded to every member, its from_selection's columns); nxr.io.adapter.kernel_from_rows; with `tiles`, the level's Weyl band folded into the kernel (nxr::signal::graphfilterbank, pipelines/spatial_band.h) |
| `meeg.carry_ends` | setup | `end_vertex`, `match` | `end_vertex` |  | The subject vertex of each end of a template's fibers: match[end_vertex]. Matches: nxr::meeg::carryEnds |
| `meeg.channel_positions` | setup | `channels`, `pick` | `positions`, `channel_index` | `position_rule`=`brainstorm`, `coil_points`=`4` | Each picked channel as one point: channels (a points manifold, with its coils and their weights when stored) and pick (an indices selection of it: which channels, in which order) -> positions [n x 3] in the channels' unit and coordinate system, and channel_index [n] (the channel each row is). position_rule brainstorm: the mean of a channel's first coil_points coil points (all of them when it has fewer; Brainstorm's GetChannelPositions), its stored point when it has no coils; stored: the stored point (the importer's: a channel's first coil). Without a pick, every channel in its stored order. Matches: nxr::meeg::channelPositions (Brainstorm's GetChannelPositions; nxr geom.topography.channel_positions; the Studio's channelPositions) |
| `meeg.coil_shapes` | setup | `channels`, `pick` | `vertices`, `faces`, `channel_index`, `shape_index` | `system`=`auto`, `details`=false | The coil shapes of the picked channels as Brainstorm draws them (figure_3d PlotCoils): channels (a points manifold with its coils) and pick -> vertices [V x 3], faces [F x 3] (each quadrilateral patch [1 2 3 4] as the triangles 1 2 3 and 1 3 4), channel_index [V] (the channel each vertex's shape belongs to) and shape_index [V] (the shape, in drawing order). system ctf (CTF, KIT, 4D, Ricoh: the quadrilateral of a channel's first four integration points, for an axial gradiometer (8 points) its pickup coil, for a 4-point magnetometer its coil; MEG REF channels only with details) or vectorview306 (a magnetometer: the points reordered 1 2 4 3 and the square scaled x2 about its centre, Brainstorm's coilScaleF 0.5; planar gradiometers, with details only: two patches each, scaled by 1.01 (..2) or 1.02 (..3) about the origin); auto is vectorview306 when a MEG GRAD channel has four points, else ctf. Matches: Brainstorm figure_3d PlotCoils (patch Faces [1 2 3 4 1] of Loc(:,1:4)) |
| `meeg.connection_weights` | setup | `fiber_counts`, `faces` | `connection_weights` | `smooth_hops`=`3` | The connection weights: the fiber counts smoothed over the mesh, smoothing · counts · smoothingᵀ, the smoothing being the mesh's smoothing step raised to smooth_hops (hops, default 3, the reference's; 0: none), the diagonal removed. Materialised vertex connectome only. Memory: about 37 non-zeros a row at 3 hops on a regular mesh; the smoothed matrix up to nF times the square of that. Matches: nxr::meeg::connectionWeights (sparse congruence: smoothing · counts · smoothingᵀ, nxr::core::sparseCongruence) |
| `meeg.eeg_montage_1005` | setup | `scalp_vertices`, `scalp_faces`, `landmarks` | `positions` | `tolerance`=`1e-07`, `max_iterations`=`100` | The 10-05 electrode positions on a closed scalp surface by the published rule: scalp_vertices [V x 3] and scalp_faces [F x 3] (0-based indices as doubles) and landmarks [4 x 3] (rows nasion, inion, LPA, RPA), all in the scalp's unit → positions [345 x 3], row k named meta.labels[k]; the 10-10 (77 names) and 10-20 (21) are subsets of the names (meta.systems). Parameters: tolerance (when Cz stops moving, a fraction of the nasion - inion distance, default 1e-7), max_iterations (a count, default 100; the node refuses when Cz has not settled). Matches: Oostenveld R, Praamstra P (2001) Clin Neurophysiol 112:713-719, the 10-05 rule; held equal to MNE-Python's spherical_1005 (eeg_positions) on a sphere (nxr::meeg::tenFive) |
| `meeg.end_connectome` | setup | `end_vertex`, `keep`? | `fiber_counts` | `n_vertices`=none | The materialised vertex matrix of fiber counts [vertices x vertices] (COO, symmetric): each kept fiber adds 1 at its two end vertices in both orders; a fiber with both ends on one vertex leaves no entry. Only on request (--over vertices --store): a partition result never forms it. Parameter n_vertices (the vertex count, no default). Matches: nxr::meeg::endConnectome |
| `meeg.end_gate` | setup | `end_distance` | `keep` | `max_end_distance_mm`=none | The distance gate: end_distance [2nF] (metres, block order) → keep [nF], 1 for a fiber with both ends within max_end_distance_mm (millimetres, the definition's; "none" keeps every fiber, as the reference does), 0 for a fiber left out. The number left out is in keep's meta (`n_left_out`, `n_fibers`, `max_end_distance_mm`) for the report and the provenance. Matches: the spec's distance gate (decided 2026-11-16); `none` reproduces tess_connectome |
| `meeg.fiber_ends` | setup | `fibers` | `end_points` | `points_per_fiber`=none | The first and the last point of each fiber: fibers [nF·nP x 3] (fiber-major, SCS metres) → end_points [2nF x 3] (row f: the first end; row nF + f: the last). Parameter points_per_fiber (nP, points, no default; >= 2). Matches: nxr::meeg::fiberEnds; the Studio's connectome.ts ends |
| `meeg.fiber_lengths` | array | `fibers` | `lengths` | `points_per_fiber`=none | each fibre's length: the sum of its segments' lengths Matches: nxr flownet's streamline lengths (Σ \|\|diff(points)\|\|); compute nxr::meeg::fiberLengths |
| `meeg.good_channels_of_type` | setup | `type`, `quality` | `pick` | `sensor_type`=`required` | The good channels of one sensor type, the channels a sensor surface is made of: type and quality (labellings of the channels: a member per channel, each member's name, e.g. MEG GRAD and good) -> pick [m] (an indices selection of the channels, ascending). sensor_type (required, no default) is MEG (MEG, MEG MAG, MEG GRAD; never MEG REF) or EEG; the two are never mixed. | `select.at_level` | chunk | `x` | `y` | `scale`=none | ONE HAT LEVEL of a multi-level field (`apply_kernel` with `levels`: row = (element · levels + level) · components + component): the rows of that level, [elements × components], pointwise in time. The level is the ladder's, one of the field's `levels`. What is left is a field of one level, as `apply_kernel` with `level` makes it Matches: a row selection of apply_kernel's [vertex × level] output (the hat level's rows of every vertex) |
| `select.bands` | array | `line`?, `grid`? | `bands` | `rule`=none, `bands`=none, `names`=none | a named band set as ONE selection of spans on the Frequency or Eigenvalue line (frequency, eigenvalue, wavelength, parts: listed; levels: a dyadic grid's Weyl bands). A single band selects; several are a band SET, never a run or a field per band. Quantities only: a bare level index is never a parameter. Matches: nxr convert.frequency and the spectral bank (D158); the Studio's coordinate charts (space.ts: linear, log10; eigenvalue, wavelength); Weyl's law on the grid's piece area; compute nxr::selection bands |
| `select.dyadic_surface` | setup | `surface` | `tiles` | `rule`=none, `finest`=none, `tree`=`subject`, `resolution`=`fsaverage5`, `atlas_finest`=none, `frame_rate`=none | The dyadic grid of a surface (equal-area bisection; level l has 2^l tiles a connected piece; the hierarchy is the closed form code >> shift). Rule `subject`: this subject's own tiles; `group`: the default subject's grid as the group tree, with the dataset's atlas definitions; `transfer`: a subject's vertices on the group tree through the registered spheres, keeping the template's codes. `finest` is the finest tile as a QUANTITY (a tile diameter, an area, a wavelength or parts per hemisphere); the depth is resolved from the grid's measured level diameters and the snapped quantity recorded. The Levi-Civita connection between neighbouring tiles is a measurement over the product of a level with itself, not part of the grid. Matches: subject: the Cortical Flow Studio engine/ladder.ts (surfaceLadder, Weyl pairing); nxr geom.ladder / geom.trees.subject_tree; Rheome +geom/surfaceladder.m; group: the Cortical Flow Studio engine/ladder.ts (surfaceLadder, Weyl pairing); nxr geom.ladder / geom.trees.subject_tree; Rheome +geom/surfaceladder.m; transfer: nxr geom.trees Template.tree_for (D127/D128): the subject's vertices on the group tree through the registered sphere |
| `select.elements` | setup | `space`, `channels_of`? | `elements` | `as`=`members` | The elements of a space (the channels of a recording, the vertices of a surface) as a set: `as: members` (each element its own member, the layout of a measurement per channel) or `as: one_member` (all elements in one member: a mean over the channels). It reads no data; `space` is the manifold, or a field on it (its first factor that is not a time line). `channels_of` (optional): a stored statistic whose channel axis is a pick (a cross-spectrum): only the picked channels are members (the others belong to none, member -1). Matches: the Studio's set selection over a manifold's elements (a channel set, a cortex) |
| `select.events.cores` | accumulate | `x`, `threshold`, `exclude`? | `spans`, `frame`, `sense`, `centre_vertex`, `centre`, `area`, `peak` | `percentile`=`98.0`, `block_frames`=`256`, `bad_segments`=`exclude` | the VORTEX CORES of a field on the frame tiling (the hatted curl at the burst frames): per frame and per sense (+1 first) the connected vertices with sense·x ≥ the threshold, joined by the mesh's edges (no merging of patches that do not touch). The threshold is the `percentile` (98, nxr's) of the stored histogram `threshold` (`core_histogram`, another run's statistic read BY NAME), derived here from its counts and edges: a core is cut from a threshold it is given. The cores are POINT EVENTS (point_events.h): a spans Selection, one member per core on its frame (members may share a frame; in the order frame, sense +1 first, lowest vertex), and per core as measurements over it: frame, sense, centre_vertex (the patch's vertex nearest its centre), centre (x y z, the \|value\|·area-weighted centroid, the surface's unit), area (Σ the patch's vertex areas, m²) and peak (the largest sense·x). Frames are independent, so the result does not depend on the chunk size. A complex x is read by its real part. Mesh: the vertices' edges from the faces of x's surface, the barycentric vertex areas, the stored positions Matches: nxr vortex._core_patches (connected patches of one sense per frame; the \|value\|·area-weighted centroid); compute nxr::select::corePatches; the threshold nxr::stats::histogram::binnedPercentile of the stored histogram |
| `select.events.patches` | accumulate | `x`, `scale`, `bursts`?, `outside`?, `exclude`?, `threshold`? | `spans`, `frame`, `burst`, `centre_vertex`, `centre`, `area`, `diameter_cm`, `characteristic_level`, `size_cm`, `relative_peak`, `home`, `summary` | `threshold`=`percentile`, `percentile`=`99.0`, `ratio`=`2.0`, `min_area`=`0.0`, `block_frames`=`256`, `bad_segments`=`exclude`, `events`=true | the SPATIAL EVENTS of a relative band power map on the frame tiling: per frame, the connected vertices of the glued mesh whose relative power is at least the threshold, joined by the mesh's edges. THE THRESHOLD is set by its false-alarm rate, measured as the time bursts' is from the envelope's own distribution: `threshold: percentile` (the default) is the `percentile` (99) of the relative power OUTSIDE the bursts, derived here from the stored distribution `threshold` (`run spatial_threshold`, another run's statistic read BY NAME; refused when made from another band, levels, reference level, shape, tiling or baseline), so about 1 % of the vertices of a frame with no event are above it; `threshold: ratio` is the named option (relative power at least `ratio` times the vertex's baseline: a single frame's relative power is about exponential, so 2 is exceeded by about 13.5 % of the vertices on noise alone). The finder is `corePatches`, which never knows its input. Stored as POINT EVENTS (point_events.h): a spans Selection, one member per patch on its frame, and per patch as measurements: frame, burst (the ordinal of the bursts Selection's span holding the frame), centre_vertex, centre (x y z, the power-weighted centroid, m), area (m²), diameter_cm (the equal-area diameter 2√(area/π)), characteristic_level (the `scale` map's level at the centre vertex and frame), size_cm (that level's centre wavelength 2π/√λ_c), relative_peak (the largest relative power in the patch). The derived threshold value is in the provenance. Patches smaller than `min_area` (m², 0: none) are dropped. The HOME MAP `home` is a statistic [vertex × (frames in a patch, good frames)]: the counts are additive over frames, the fraction is derived at read; a vertex is in a patch when its relative power is at least the threshold (min_area drops events, not vertices). Frames are independent, so the result does not depend on the chunk or the block. MEMORY: V × block_frames doubles a few times over Matches: compute nxr::select::corePatches (the vortex cores' patch finder, on relative power instead of the curl); decisions 1-4 of docs/specs/2026-11-14-spatial-events.md |

| `select.scale` | chunk | `x` | `y` | `transform`=`auto`, `modes`=`0`, `order`=`0`, `tolerance`=`0.01` | the CHARACTERISTIC LEVEL of each vertex and frame (): x is the band power of a multi-level field (`apply_kernel` with `levels`, then `power`); at each vertex the level whose power over the squared L2 norm of its atom is the largest, as the ladder's level (a float). The atom of a vertex at a level is the operator's column there (the level's hat applied to the native sources, read at that glued vertex), its norm the Euclidean norm of that column over the native vertices, computed exactly in preparation (the band applied to the identity, a block of 256 columns at a time; MEMORY: the glued vertices × 256 doubles; TIME: one band application to as many columns as the surface has vertices, per level). So a blob of a level's own size gives its largest normalised power at that level, and white noise the same at every level. Pointwise in time and in space (the maximum is over the level axis); the lowest level on a tie. `transform`, `modes`, `order`, `tolerance` are the bands' (apply_kernel's: the same operators). The level in centimetres is read at the events (2π/√λ_c of the level's hat centre) Matches: Lindeberg (1998) scale selection with L2-normalised responses (spatial-events spec, decision 4); compute nxr::select::scale_selection::selectLevel; the atoms are nxr `vortex_cores.hat_operator`'s columns (the bands of apply_kernel) |

Per tile, sense and STAGE (`burst`: every step; `onset`, `within`, `offset`: the steps whose frame starts inside that stage's spans, the inputs of those names): the crossings' unit vectors added (a 3-D tangent vector at the tile's centre) and their number. ONE MEASUREMENT over the level's tiles, `tile_crossings`, [rows × members × 4]: rows 2i and 2i+1 are stage i's senses +1 and −1; members are the level's tiles then a `bridge` member (the last: crossings whose nearest vertex is on the callosal bridge, their unit vectors added in 3-D); components the vector (crossing_sum_x/y/z) then the count (crossings). R = \|S\|/n and the unbiased rho2 = (\|S\|² − n)/(n (n − 1)) are DERIVED at read, never stored. Reads the cores' list, not the chunks Matches: nxr vortex_cores.Tiles.crossings (a track's steps in one tile, carried to the tile centre by the vector heat method, added, made a unit vector; per tile and sense); compute nxr::select::track_crossings, nxr::select::leviCivita |
| `select.time_grid` | setup | `line`, `event`? | `grid` | `rule`=none, `duration`=none, `band`=none, `frames_per_tile`=none, `frames_per_cycle`=none, `origin`=none, `cycles`=none, `window`=none, `step`=none, `segment`=none, `overlap`=none, `preset`=none, `method`=none, `voices`=none, `range`=none, `f_min`=none, `f_max`=none | The members of a time line's grid: member i is [origin + i hop, origin + i hop + width), counted in the line's samples. One rule family: `tiles` (a duration: the first level whose 2^k-sample tile holds it), `band` (a band in Hz: the tile holding 4 cycles of its centre, the Studio's fitLevelOf), `frames` (a band and frames_per_tile, a power of two, or frames_per_cycle: the frame grid of a band), `constant_q` (a frequency range and voices: the Studio's constant-Q ladder), `segments` (a duration and an overlap: Welch's segments), `windows` (a window and a step, each snapped to 2^k samples) and `chunks` (2^15 samples). `origin` is an option: the line's first sample (default), a clock time ("12.5 s") or `event` (the first member of the spans selection given as `event`). Every parameter is a quantity: a bare level index is never a parameter. The level is resolved in closed form and the SNAPPED quantity (what the level actually is) is recorded. A grid made by tiles, band or frames is one LEVEL of the line's dyadic time grid: nothing per level is stored. Matches: the Cortical Flow Studio's time grid (jointTime.ts fitLevelOf, tower frames at the band's level), Rheome's natural_level and jointladder, scipy.signal.welch's segments; compute nxr::selection::time_grid, time_rule, constant_q_design |

| `signal.analytic_bands` | chunk | `x`, `channels_of`? | `z` | `bands`=`[]`, `channel_types`=`["MEG", "MEG MAG", "MEG GRAD", "EEG", "SEEG", "ECOG"]` | the analytic signal of each band (Meyer bands), with the halo the narrowest band needs Matches: the Studio's Signal chain meyerBand (toolbox/wavelets/dyadicFrame.ts); compute nxr::signal::wtBlock |
| `signal.analytic_frames` | chunk | `x`, `tiling`, `within`? | `y` | `band`=none, `shape`=`morlet`, `half_width`=`0.3333333333333333`, `frames_per_cycle`=none, `frames_per_tile`=none, `origin`=none, `tolerance`=`1e-06` | the analytic signal of a band of a real field read at the FRAME TILING (a closed-form spans Selection of frames, `select.time_grid` rule frames: a frame's time is its tile's start): ONE step, the band's wavelet transform of the chunk's block evaluated at each frame's (non-integer) sample position, a sum over the band's bins, never a signal on every sample interpolated. The band is `band` [lo, hi] Hz with its `shape` (morlet \| meyer, `half_width` octaves for meyer's edges), the analytic signal of gain 2 as `analytic`. The block is the chunk with the halo the band's response needs (its impulse response down to `tolerance` of its L1 norm, default 1e-6: timefilterbank::haloOf), so the result does not depend on the chunk size; a frame belongs to the chunk holding the sample at or before it. The output's columns are FRAMES (axis `frames`): the steps after it are pointwise in time (a linear map, a form, \|x\|², a series kept) and fold frames; a step that reads the samples' own time refuses it. With `within` (a spans Selection of the recording's time line: the bursts, a stage) only the frames inside a span are GOOD (the steps after it leave the others out); without it every frame is. Beyond the recording the signal reads 0 Matches: nxr vortex.band_at_frames (the band's analytic signal at the frames); here the band's wavelet `wt(bank, member, window, instants)` (nxr::signal, Morlet or Meyer, the Studio's gains) evaluated at the START of each frame, exactly (no interpolation) |

Rows atom-major (row = atom x channels + channel), one group of rows a width over its own frames. A frame belongs to the chunk holding its sample; the block carries the halo the widest atom needs (its response down to `tolerance` of its L1 norm), so the series does not depend on the chunk size. Frames on a bad sample are NaN. The magnitude is taken here, as the series leaves the loop (holding it complex would double it; nothing after reads its phase: the fit reads the samples). MEMORY of one block, checked against `budget` (bytes) before any data flows and refused with the remedy: channels x (the padded block x 8 + its spectrum x 16) + the largest width's atoms x channels x the block's frames x 4. THE RUN holds each width's \|W\| over the span: Σ over widths of atoms x channels x (rate / decimation) x 4 bytes a second; that times the span asked, plus the block, is checked against `budget` on the first block (before anything is held) and refused with both figures, the longest span that fits and the remedies. Matches: the reference detector's channel_atoms (unit-energy atoms of free width; its grid; each width on its own band, at its own rate); compute nxr::signal::timefilterbank (Family::Gabor, gaborGrid; spectrum), nxr::signal::wtDecimated |

| `signal.source_planes` | array | `spectrum`, `kernel` | `energy`, `pairs` | `pairs`=`3` | the quadrature spectrum of the sources: per band the quadrature fraction, the energy per source and the strongest quadrature pairs, from the sensors' cross-spectrum and a kernel Matches: nxr.spectral.lagged (im_fraction, im_rows, planes); compute nxr::signal |

| `signal.tile_flow` | array | `spectra`, `operator`, `frequency` | `pair_flow`, `tile_power` | `frequency_normalisation`=none, `support_floor`=none | the whole run's cross-spectrum of the tiles' currents per atom: the ingredients of the edge flow, the lag and the speed (derived at read) Matches: nxr flownet's Stot (the per-segment C = w wᴴ traced over components, summed): here the same sums from the factored cross-spectrum; compute nxr::signal::pairFlow |

| `signal.tile_time_cells` | array | `spectra`, `operator`, `frequency`, `grid`, `product` | `pair_cells`, `tile_cells` | `frequency_normalisation`=none, `support_floor`=none, `cell_width`=none | the tiles' cross-spectrum of each atom summed over the tiles of a stored time grid: the sums the sign-flip test and its mean edge flow read (measurements over the grid x atoms) Matches: nxr flownet's per-segment C = w wᴴ traced over components, here per tile of a stored time grid and rolled up to each atom's own window at the test; compute nxr::signal::timeCellPairFlow |

| `stats.aperiodic_fit` | array | `power` | `fit` | `knee`=none, `fit_range`=none, `iterations`=none, `threshold`=none | the aperiodic background of each spectrum (specparam's aperiodic model, with or without a knee) Matches: nxr nxr.spectral.aperiodic.fit (the lab's specparam port); compute nxr::signal::fitAperiodic |
| `stats.connectomeFeature` | array | `matrices`, `bands` | `feature` |  | the connectome feature of a person: the bands' region x region matrices stacked on a band axis Matches: the MEG fingerprinting release's connectome (68 x 68 a band, six bands; read with the upper triangle and its diagonal, 4_AEC_fingerprinting_*); compute nxr::stats::connectomeFeature |
| `stats.correlation` | array | `covariance` | `correlation` | `measure`=`correlation`, `warnings`=`[]` | Pearson's correlation of every pair of rows, from their covariance Matches: MATLAB corrcoef, Brainstorm's bst_corrn (of 2018-10-12), numpy corrcoef; compute nxr::stats::correlation |
| `stats.cov` | accumulate | `x` | `covariance` | `remove_mean`=true, `divisor`=`samples_minus_one`, `axis`=`row` | the covariance of a series' rows over the run's span (one block, its mean removed) Matches: MATLAB cov / numpy cov of the span's samples (observations in the columns); compute nxr::stats::CovarianceEstimate |
| `stats.featureTable` | array | `target`, `database` | `table` | `vector`=`flatten` | the members' feature vectors from their stored features, the target's then the database's Matches: the release's feature vectors (megFingerprinting 4_PSD_ and 4_AEC_fingerprinting_*, cell 4); nxr::stats::featureTable |
| `stats.identification` | array | `table` | `correlation`, `self`, `accuracy`, `edgewise` | `self_identifiability`=`all` | the identification of a cohort's members from two feature vectors each: correlation, accuracy both ways, self-identifiability and the edgewise reliability Matches: the release's notebooks (megFingerprinting 4_PSD_fingerprinting_within_session, cells 6, 13, 16, 20); nxr::stats::identification |
| `stats.identificationCurve` | array | `components`, `scores`, `centring` | `curve`, `reconstructed_self`, `reconstructed_edgewise` | `steps`=`notebook`, `self_identifiability`=`all` | the identification of a cohort's PCA reconstructions at increasing numbers of components, and the best one's edgewise reliability Matches: the release's notebooks (megFingerprinting 4_PSD_fingerprinting_within_session, cells 8, 10, 13, 16-20) with an exact SVD in place of scikit-learn's randomised solver; nxr::stats::identificationCurve |
| `stats.network_sign_flip` | array | `pair_cells`, `tile_cells`, `pairs` | `consistency` | `patterns`=none, `seed`=none, `min_streamlines`=none, `distance_bin_edges`=none | the reference's nulls of the flow through the network: the sign-flip (time reversal) test of each pair's edge flow over the cells with its family-wise maximum, and the distance-matched not-joined pairs as the control Matches: nxr flownet's flip (sign flip over segments, \|null\| >= \|obs\|, family-wise maximum on the sums normalised by Σ\|F\|) and its distance-matched control (rng.choice per np.digitize bin), numpy default_rng bit for bit; compute nxr::stats::networkSignFlip, distanceMatchedControl |
| `stats.pca` | array | `x` | `components`, `scores`, `variance`, `centring` | `members`=none, `scale`=`none` | the principal components across the members of a table of measurements, by the thin SVD of the centred table Matches: scikit-learn's PCA (svd_solver full); nxr::stats |
| `stats.run_replication` | array | `first`, `second`, `pairs` | `replication` | `min_streamlines`=none | run-to-run replication of the flow through the network: per atom the correlation of two runs' edge flows over the joined pairs and over the not-joined pairs Matches: nxr's replication of the flow through the fibres (views/netfig: np.corrcoef of run 1's and run 2's F_k over the joined and the not-joined pairs) |
| `stats.sign_flip_consistency` | array | `edge_cells`?, `vertex_cells`?, `whole_edge_cells`?, `whole_vertex_cells`? | `consistency`, `consistency_summary`, `whole_consistency`, `whole_consistency_summary` | `measure_suffix`=`, `elements`=none, `patterns`=none, `seed`=none, `cells_per_flip`=none | the sign-flip (time-reversal) test of the direction's consistency over each atom's own time cells (the stored tiles rolled up to the atom's own window), per element, with a family-wise maximum Matches: nxr's flow maps flip_test (nxr's flow analysis: R1, per-vertex p, family-wise maximum, numpy default_rng); compute nxr::stats::signFlipConsistency, NumpyGenerator |

## synthesis

| node | kind | inputs (optional marked) | outputs | parameters (defaults) | what it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `synthesis.lagfree` | chunk | `x`, `psd`, `psd_channel_mean`, `cross_spectrum`, `power_series` | `y` | `band`=none, `shape`=`morlet`, `half_width`=`0.3333333333333333`, `taps_half`=`0`, `seed`=`0` | ONE LAG-FREE DRAW, UNMIXED, in place of the recording: per channel of the stored cross-spectrum one stream of Gaussian noise with the recording's own mean spectrum (the stored Welch PSD over those channels: never flat), scaled in time to the data's tile power (`power_series`) over the draw's expected power through the band's analytic gain, so the mixed draw's analytic signal has the data's band envelope. A function of the SAMPLE INDEX (a counter-based generator of `seed`): the draw does not depend on the chunk size; another `seed` is another draw. x is the recording's SHAPE (rows, rate, samples; `read: shape`): no sample is read. Channels the cross-spectrum does not cover are zero. The output AWAITS the zero-lag mixing (`synthesis.lagfree_mixing`), applied once in the first linear map (apply_kernel's `pre_operator`): it commutes with every linear time step before it (spec docs/specs/2026-11-17-surrogates.md, section 4). `taps_half` 0: from the PSD's resolution (half = fs / (2 df), at most 4096) Matches: Rheome +rheome/+cores lagfreenull and envelopenull (Gaussian noise with the data's mean spectrum, rescaled to the data's one-cycle envelope; the mixing is applied later, composed into the spatial operator); compute nxr::synthesis (shapedNoiseBlock, spectrumShapingTaps, analyticGainPower, envelopeScale, interpolateTileSeries); the scale is pointwise (expected, not realised) |
| `synthesis.lagfree_mixing` | setup | `cross_spectrum` | `mixing` |  | the ZERO-LAG MIXING of the band: the symmetric square root of the real part of the stored cross-spectrum at unit mean channel variance, an operator [M × M] over the cross-spectrum's channels (meta.channels, in order) with its provenance (meta.provenance: the cross-spectrum's id and name). A surrogate's unmixed draw awaits it; it is composed ONCE into the first linear map of the chain (apply_kernel's `pre_operator`), never applied per sample Matches: Rheome +rheome/+cores lagfreenull (Rh = the symmetric square root of the zero-lag covariance), pairsqrt; compute nxr::synthesis::zeroLagMixing |
| `synthesis.lagfree_pairs` | setup | `recording`, `bursts`, `psd` | `per_burst`, `run` | `windows`=none, `band`=none, `shape`=none, `half_width`=none, `draws`=`1000`, `seed`=`0` | per burst, the lagged share of its sensors' second moment against lag-free Wishart draws of its own zero-lag second moment and degrees of freedom; and the run's mean share against the draws' Matches: Rheome +rheome/+cores pairnull, pairshare, pairdof, bh, tilepq; compute nxr::synthesis::lagfreeSecondMomentDraw, laggedShare, effectiveBandwidth; nxr::stats::fixedDrawPs, benjaminiHochbergQ, compareMeanOverMembers |
